thesis: Micron's 60-day rally reflects AI/HBM demand tailwinds: management disclosed roughly $100B in remaining obligations under 16 multi-year customer supply agreements as of June, aimed at making DRAM/HBM earnings less cyclical, and sell-side coverage (BofA, UBS) expects gross margins to hold near the mid-80% range through fiscal 2027. Fiscal Q4 earnings land Sept. 30 and are still pending, so the strongest confirming catalyst hasn't printed yet. Bears (Michael Burry, Martin Shkreli) are shorting on the view that this is still a cyclical memory business whose HBM-driven margin expansion will unwind once new supply (including China's CXMT) comes online -- a real counter-case this run's sourced research does not fully resolve either way. A USITC investigation into Netlist patent claims against Micron's memory products was formally instituted Sept. 24, but no hearing or ruling date has been set yet.
invalidation: Sept. 30 earnings/guidance disappoints on HBM allocation or gross-margin trajectory, or memory pricing rolls over as new supply comes online.

thesis: Hafnia reported a record $277.8M Q2 net profit (strongest since Q3 2022), cut net loan-to-value from 20.2% to 13%, and is paying out 90% of profit as dividends (annualized yield around 21% at the time of the print) on the back of Persian Gulf/Red Sea shipping disruptions widening ton-miles for product tankers. It is also compounding a strategic equity stake in TORM (now roughly 20%) funded from its own cash flow, not new share issuance. Counter-case: the strong tanker rates are largely geopolitically driven (Gulf/Red Sea disruption) rather than a structural change to the business, so de-escalation could compress the current rate environment; management itself frames Q3/Q4 as constructive 'with the caveat that we are sitting in a very politically driven environment.' The CEO transition (Michael Skov to Søren Steenberg Jensen) was announced in June as a planned succession with the outgoing CEO moving to the board, not tied to any operational problem.
invalidation: Middle East/Red Sea shipping disruptions resolve and TCE rates normalize sharply lower, or the dividend payout ratio is cut.
